key_insight: Local atomic-swap tests indicate that GNN feature rankings can capture physically meaningful neighbor-shell effects even under deliberate overfitting.
engineering_relevance: Perturbation-based validation can help engineers assess whether materials-model explanations reflect local chemistry rather than only compositional correlations.
method: Train a deliberately overfit, physics-aware GNN ensemble on DFT-derived CoMoFeNiCu decomposition enthalpies.
Constrain output weights to encode feature importance.
Swap atoms at individual sites and re-rank features to test spatial sensitivity.
evidence_signal: Across three stoichiometries with approximately 900 binary and 4,500 ternary decomposition pathways, attribution changes showed spatial decay consistent with the GNN interaction cutoff.
watch_item: Validation is limited to a deliberately overfit model in one alloy system; generalization across chemistries and compositions remains untested.
paper_title: Validating Graph Neural Network Feature Attribution Through Local Perturbations: A Study on CoMoFeNiCu Decomposition Enthalpy
